stories.title: Trump faces new political reality as Democrats vow investigations
summary: President Donald Trump was left to grapple on Thursday with the stinging rebuke from voters after a midterm election rout, while triumphant Democrats vowed to lower prices and combat the “cartel” within the White House in the new Congress.
It will be the first time that Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with a Democratic-controlled Congress in both chambers.

Trump had cast the midterm elections as a referendum on the first half of his second four-year stint in the White House, repeatedly urging his Republican base to “pretend I’m on the ballot”, a message that Democratic Party leaders were happy to amplify.

stories.title: Pakistan, UK agree to deepen cooperation in security, trade and migration
summary: Pakistan and the United Kingdom on Thursday agreed to deepen cooperation in multiple areas, according to the Foreign Office (FO).

Islamabad and London have also been engaged in the Enhanced Strategic Dialogue since 2011, which has deepened and broadened the dialogue between the two countries, covering areas such as trade, economic growth and development, cultural cooperation, security, and education.

stories.title: Lahore’s air pollution a year-round problem, worsened by winter and agricultural burning: report
summary: On Monday, air pollution in Lahore reached hazardous levels, with the Air Quality Index (AQI) crossing 530 and fine particulate matter (PM2.5) concentrations climbing to 343 micrograms per cubic metre.

Citing the Urban Unit’s 2023 Lahore emissions inventory, which was based on 2020–21 data, the report said that transport accounted for about 35pc of the city’s PM2.5 emissions, compared with 33pc from crop-residue burning, 29pc from waste burning and three per cent from industry.

Alongside monitoring infrastructure, the Punjab government has been implementing a multi-sectoral air pollution reduction strategy targeting transport, industrial emissions, brick kilns and agricultural burning.

stories.title: PM directs cancellation of petrol pump licences over failure to facilitate fuel subsidy beneficiaries
summary: The meeting was informed that 15,519,282 citizens had registered under the subsidy scheme so far, including 15.06 million motorcycle owners and 449,000 owners of vehicles with engine capacities of up to 800cc.
PM Shehbaz announced a relief scheme in September for owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles with engine capacities of up to 800cc.

Under the scheme, owners of two- and three-wheeled vehicles are eligible for a subsidy of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres, while owners of vehicles with engine capacities of up to 800cc are entitled to the same subsidy on a monthly quota of 30 litres.

stories.title: Minister says electoral reforms panel to have 2 members each from PML-N, PPP and PTI
summary: The ruling PML-N, its coalition partner PPP and the opposition PTI will each get two seats on the proposed Parliamentary Committee on Electoral Reforms (PCER), Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said on Thursday.
He said the opposition leader should nominate representatives to the committee on electoral reforms and submit the names to the Speaker’s Office.

During the meeting, the PPP delegation invited the opposition to participate in the parliamentary committee to promote consultation and discussion among parliamentary representatives on electoral reforms.

stories.title: New LPG policy
summary: LPG, long considered the poor man’s fuel, is now what many middle-class families use for cooking and heating.
Gas rationing due to shortages caused by dwindling domestic gas reserves, together with increasing tariffs on imported RLNG, is boosting the demand for LPG.

This year, as the petroleum minister told the National Assembly last month, the closure of the western borders has disrupted import shipments, which account for 70pc of LPG imports, exacerbating the shortages.

stories.title: New wave of bomb threats hits passenger flights across Europe
summary: Airlines across Europe received a series of bomb threats on Thursday morning for the second time this week, forcing many to make unplanned or escorted landings, although none of the threats immediately proved to be genuine.
Bulgarian officials reported three aircraft making emergency landings in the Balkan country because of bomb threats.
On Tuesday, at least seven flights and a cruise ship received bomb threats, causing disruption at airports across Europe, although no devices were discovered.

stories.title: Cristiano Ronaldo announces international retirement
summary: Cristiano Ronaldo announced his intention to retire from the Portugal national team on Thursday in a social media post, bringing to an end one of the most illustrious international careers in the history of football.

Ronaldo captained the team to their first major trophy at Euro 2016 and helped them win the 2019 and 2025 Nations Leagues. “It was not an easy decision, because there are decisions that are not made only with the head.
Ronaldo has made 234 appearances for Portugal and scored 146 goals.

stories.title: ECP sets Feb 7 as polling date for first phase of Punjab local govt elections; KP polls delayed
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Thursday decided to hold the first phase of local government elections in Punjab on Feb 7, 2027, in view of fog and weather conditions, while polls in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa were postponed until further orders.
It was further decided that the first phase of local government elections in Punjab will be held with the polling date set as Feb 7, 2027.
After deliberation, it was decided that in view of the said order, holding local government elections in the remaining districts of KP was no longer possible.

stories.title: FCC bars PHC from hearing cases related to PTI workers' preventive detention
summary: The FCC restrained the high court from proceeding further on the cases and decided to issue notices to the parties with a direction that they may also file their pleas before the superior court.

KP Advocate General Sanaullah Khan, who pleaded the case before the FCC on behalf of the provincial government, told Dawn that the PHC’s orders had been challenged under Article 245 of the Constitution, which provides for calling in armed forces in aid of civil forces.

He cited clause 3 of the provision, arguing that a high court could not “directly entertain a case under Article 199 of the Constitution since it cannot exercise its jurisdiction in relation to any area in which the armed forces are acting in aid of the civil power”.

stories.title: France braces for demonstrations as trade unions strike
summary: Hundreds of thousands of people are expected to take to the streets across France on Thursday, as unions hold strikes alongside student-led demonstrations that have gripped the country for weeks.

The high school student movement that began with youth protesting dismal learning conditions has coincided with widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality, which culminated on October 17 in the worst rioting France has seen in years.
Similar protests have sparked in other European countries in recent weeks with youth-led demonstrations seen in Denmark, Germany and Italy.

stories.title: PTA dismisses 'fake and misleading' notification claiming TikTok banned in Pakistan
summary: The Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) on Thursday dismissed reports of a ban on video-sharing platform TikTok as “false and misleading”, clarifying that no notification to that effect had been issued.

In a post on social media platform X, the authority said that a fake notification regarding an alleged ban on TikTok was being circulated on social media. “PTA clarifies that no such notification has been issued, and the circulating information is false and misleading,” it said.
Eventually, the PTA had lifted the ban in November 2021 following assurances by TikTok that it would “control” the uploading and dissemination of “immoral and indecent content” on the app.

stories.title: Trump says Hegseth doing 'a very good job' as questions swirl about defence secretary's future
summary: US President Donald Trump backed Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth a day after Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in midterm elections that reflected voter anger over the war on Iran.
The Defence Department said Hegseth was “100 percent committed” to leading the Pentagon until the end of Trump’s term, which ends on Jan.

Asked whether he wanted Hegseth to fill Blackburn’s seat, Trump said: “Well, I think, I think he’s doing a very good job, and I actually think he’d be very popular if he did that.” “But I haven’t heard that at all,” Trump told reporters.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz orders cancellation of petrol pump licences over denial of fuel subsidies
summary: Shehbaz directed the relevant authorities to ensure that registered beneficiaries faced no hurdles in obtaining subsidised fuel and that petrol pumps complied with the government's instructions.
On September 14, the Economic Coordination Committee of the Cabinet had set aside Rs75 billion for the Prime Minister's Fuel Relief Scheme.
The Economic Coordination Committee (ECC), chaired by Finance Minister Muhammad Aurangzeb, had approved the Prime Minister's Fuel Relief Scheme on September 14.

stories.title: Restoration of peace, elimination of corruption major challenges in Malakand division: PPP
summary: Addressing a press conference at Swat Press Club, he said PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari had entrusted him with the responsibility of provincial information secretary.

Bilawal Bhutto Zardari had made efforts to ensure the continuation of a democratic government in the province and avoid the imposition of governor’s rule, but all other options were exhausted before the decision was taken.
Dr Haider Ali Khan said restoring peace in the province was imperative, as peace was essential for creating employment opportunities and ensuring public prosperity.

stories.title: Governor Kundi vows to prioritise KP’s security, uplift
summary: DERA ISMAIL KHAN: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Governor Faisal Karim Kundi on Wednesday said that the fight against terrorism remained the top priority of the provincial government, followed by efforts to ensure the restoration of peace and bring prosperity to the province.
About the Chashma Right Bank Canal breach, he said the authorities had been given a deadline of November 15 to 20 to restore water supply through the canal.

Dera Division Commissioner Dawood Khan, the regional police officer, the deputy commissioner, the district police officer, assistant commissioners and heads of various government departments attended the meeting.

stories.title: Ronaldo calls time on Portugal career
summary: The 41-year-old said that he ‌would 'hand back the number ‌7 shirt' after the November international break.
Ronaldo has made 234 appearances for Portugal and scored 146 goals.
He holds the all-time record for international ⁠appearances and for ⁠international goals.

stories.title: PIDCL stopped from finalising tender for Latifabad flyover project in Hyderabad
summary: They stated in their petition that the roundabout at the site did not experience flow of heavy traffic or congestion that could necessitate construction of a major flyover there.

The petitioners claimed that the proposed flyover construction might substantially alter the existing road configuration, affect adjoining residential accommodations and commercial activities, create noise, dust and other environmental impacts.
They said the flyover project involved a cost of over Rs660m whereas the roundabout widening and installation of traffic signal project was already in progress and nearing completion.

stories.title: Owono devastated by De Miguel's death
summary: FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono said Wednesday he is enduring the "hardest days of my life" after the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel, whom he collided with during a Spanish second division match on Monday.
"After the tragic news of the death of Tenerife player Jesus de Miguel, the game... this Saturday November 7, at Nuevo Los Carmenes (stadium), has been postponed," said Granada in a statement.
The Spanish football federation postponed all Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina matches this week as a mark of respect following De Miguel's death.

stories.title: Islamabad High Court questions acquittal of former EOBI chief in corruption case
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court has questioned the acquittal of the former chairman of Employees Old-Age Benefits Institution (EOBI), the prime suspect in a Rs40 billion corruption case, and summoned him along with other accused to appear in person on Nov 20.

Justice Shahrukh Arjumand, hearing a criminal appeal filed by EOBI against the acquittal, issued notices to all respondents after hearing arguments challenging the trial court’s decision to acquit them in the corruption case.

During the hearing on Nov 2, EOBI’s counsel Aftab Alam Yasir argued that the impugned judgment had been passed without proper justification, despite allegations of serious financial irregularities in the institution’s investments.

stories.title: National Assembly body raps NHA chief over ‘false’ report on N-65
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Nati­onal Assembly Standing Committee on Commu­nications has taken Nati­onal Highway Authority (NHA) Chairman Asadu­llah Khan to task for delays in completing major highways, including the Sukkur-Shikarpur road (N-65) and the Dera Murad Jamali Bypass.
He said the NHA had been given two months at the last meeting to get the road repaired, but the authority had done nothing. “Rather, a false report was presented before the committee.
Taking serious notice, the committee directed the NHA to submit a comprehensive, project-wise report identifying cases of substandard construction and projects undertaken without adequate planning.

stories.title: Metropolitan Corporation Islamabad closes G-10 weekly, ladies bazaars permanently
summary: Accordingly, the temporarily established weekly (Sunday) bazaar and women’s bazaar at G-10 right of way are permanently closed with immediate effect,” read a notification issued by the MCI.

It is relevant to note that the CDA’s Development Working Party (DWP) approved a PC-I worth Rs24.5 billion for the construction of 11th Avenue, stretching from Margalla Avenue to Karnal Sher Khan Road.
However, sources said the CDA was considering executing the project in two phases.

stories.title: FIA Islamabad Zone books 12 deportees from Libya in human trafficking case
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) has registered a human trafficking case against 12 Pakistani nationals deported from Libya, and initiated action against agents allegedly involved in sending them to Italy illegally.

According to the FIA Islamabad Zone, the deportees were handed over by FIA Immigration at Islamabad Airport to the Anti-Human Trafficking Circle Rawalpindi for further legal proceedings, after which the case was registered.
The FIA Islamabad Zone said it remains committed to continuing legal action against elements involved in human smuggling and illegal migration.

stories.title: Kane extends contract with Bayern Munich
summary: Harry Kane said he felt "right at home" after he signed a two-year extension at Bayern Munich, keeping the Ballon d'Or winner at the club until 2029, the German champions announced on Thursday.

Bayern sporting director Christoph Freund said the club were "absolutely delighted" to extend Kane's deal, adding: "With Harry Kane we have the Ballon d'Or winner on the pitch -- a team player, a leader, the best all-round striker in the world.
'Best place possible' Much as Premier League sides might have dreamed of luring him back to England, Kane's longer-term Bayern future has never been in doubt.

stories.title: Lahore High court moved for transparency in e-challan system
summary: The application filed by Advocate Azhar Siddique alleges that traffic fines are being imposed without proper identification of vehicles and human verification, resulting in citizens being penalised for violations committed by other motorists.
It refers to the case of a Gujrat resident whose 2018 model car received five e-challans for traffic violations in Lahore.
The application claims the citizen travelled from Naran to Gujrat and maintained that his vehicle was not in Lahore on the dates of the alleged violations.

stories.title: Crackdown on canal water theft: Punjab Irrigation Dept lodges 200 FIRs, resulting in 63 arrests
summary: LAHORE: Grappling with a crippling 22pc water shortage for the ongoing Rabi season, the Punjab Irrigation Department has lodged 200 first information reports (FIRs), resulting in arrest of 63 individuals, for water theft since mid-October, as part of a province-wide crackdown.
The Punjab irrigation authorities aim to curb illegal diversions and ensure equitable water distribution for wheat crop, particularly for vulnerable farmers stationed at the canal tail-ends.
Bahawalpur irrigation zone tops the list with 621 cases of tampered water outlets (mogas), followed by Faisalabad zone with 326 and Lahore with 121 cases.

stories.title: Shafay ‘distances’ himself from Salik
summary: The PML-Q has only one minister in the Punjab cabinet — Shafay Hussain.
On Tuesday, Ms Nawaz served a Rs5 billion defamation notice on Salik over his corruption allegations against her government, demanding that he retract his remarks.

Meanwhile, Ms Bokhari asked Mr Salik to substantiate his corruption allegations or apologise, saying he could not enjoy the privileges of being part of the government while simultaneously engaging in political mudslinging.

stories.title: Three children die in Peshawar cylinder explosion
summary: Three children died after a cylinder explosion on Pajaggi Road in Peshawar on Thursday, while a woman and another child remained under treatment at Lady Reading Hospital (LRH), hospital spokesperson Muhammad Asim said.
According to Asim, five people injured in the explosion were shifted to the hospital, where three children succumbed to their injuries.
On July 16, at least 10 people suffered severe burn injuries when a gas cylinder exploded at a sweets and fast food shop near Chungi No 5 in Burewala, triggering panic in the area.

stories.title: ECP announces February 7 for Punjab LG polls, suspends K-P election process
summary: A four-member bench headed by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja heard the case concerning local government elections in Punjab.
The Punjab chief secretary informed the commission that preparations for the local government elections had been completed.

Later, in a short order issued by the commission, the Punjab chief secretary informed the ECP that consultations between the provincial government's committee and the commission had earlier resulted in an understanding to hold the elections between December and January.

stories.title: Economic Coordination Committee clears Rs380bn grants
summary: ISLAMABAD: The Economic Coordination Committee (ECC) of the cabinet on Wednesday approved supplementary grants worth about Rs380 billion, including Rs275bn for five major water projects facing financial constraints, and around Rs84bn for the country’s armed forces.
An official statement said the ECC approved three summaries submitted by the Defence Division.

Approves Rs275bn for five water projects, Rs84bn for armed forces The ECC also approved supplementary grants of Rs275bn for important water sector projects currently under implementation and facing financial constraints under the Ministry of Water Resources.

stories.title: Chief Ministers Bugti, Maryam agree on joint efforts for safe cities in Balochistan
summary: QUETTA: Balochistan Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti and his Punjab counterpart Maryam Nawaz have agreed to strengthen cooperation to make Safe City projects in Balochistan more effective, operational and aligned with modern security requirements.

Following a request from Mr Bugti, the Punjab chief minister issued directives to the relevant authorities to provide institutional support and assistance to strengthen the Balochistan Safe City Authority.

He thanked the Punjab chief minister and the Punjab Safe City Authority for extending cooperation and support to Balochistan, saying institutional collaboration and the exchange of experience between provinces would help achieve shared public safety objectives.

stories.title: NAB summons Fazl’s son in Pakistan Post case
summary: ISLAMABAD: The National Accountability Bureau (NAB) has summoned former federal minister for communication Asad Mahmood, who is the son of JUI-F president Maulana Fazlur Rehman, for alleged irregularities in 4,252 appointments at Pakistan Post during his 2022-23 term.
According to a NAB notice, the bureau is investigating alleged irregularities in appointments made at Pakistan Post during Mr Mahmood’s tenure as federal minister between 2022 and 2023.

Bureau to probe excessive appointments allegedly in violation of cabinet committee’s direction Mr Mahmood had served as federal minister during the last PML-N-led Pakistan Democratic Movement (PDM) government in 2022-23.

stories.title: PSX extends rally for second session, gains over 3,400 points
summary: The Pakistan Stock Exchange extended its bullish run on Thursday, with the benchmark KSE-100 index climbing to 175,464.01 by midday, up 3,450.53 points or 2.01% from the previous close of 172,013.48.
The gains build on Wednesday’s strong session, when the KSE-100 rose nearly 4,000 points to close at 172,013.48 amid broad-based buying.
The market has now moved firmly above the 175,000 level during the day, though it has eased slightly from the session high.

stories.title: Number of blue passports brought down to 49,000 from 74,000, DG says
summary: The existing mechanism for issuance of passports, institutional performance, security features and facilities being provided to the public came under discussion during the meeting.

Senate deputy chairman lauds promotion of using technology to facilitate public Mr Nasar appreciated the government’s initiatives aimed at improving the passport issuance system, promoting the use of modern technology and enhancing public facilitation.

Mr Nasar said the use of modern technology, digital systems and automation should be expanded at all stages of passport issuance to make the entire process, from submission of an application to passport delivery, faster, more transparent and accessible.

stories.title: PCB announces Pakistan-Sri Lanka Test ticket prices
summary: Ticket sales for Pakistan’s opening Test against Sri Lanka will begin on Friday, November 6, the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) announced.
The first Test will be played in Rawalpindi from November 9-13, with the second scheduled in Lahore from November 17-21.
The PCB said ticket sale details for the Lahore Test would be announced at a later date.

stories.title: FCC rejects JUI-F appeal against election of its own lawmaker
summary: During the hearing, counsel for JUI-F informed the court that the party had submitted four names for reserved seats.
The counsel argued that the ECP could not make changes to the list submitted by a political party for reserved seats. “This is a unique case in Pakistan's history,” the JUI-F lawyer said.
JUI-F challenges own lawmaker’s election The JUI-F challenged the election of Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa (K-P) Assembly member Sadaf, elected on the reserved seats for women, in the Supreme Court.
